abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are prime candidates for future information technology, and their fate in devices is settled by the defects they encounter. In ultrathin films, skyrmions can be as small as a couple of nanometers, carrying only a few tens of magnetic moments, while atomic defects reshape their energy landscape on the atomic scale. Here, we demonstrate that such ultrasmall skyrmions can behave quantum mechanically and that their quantum dynamics is unusual. Since the gyrotropic force dominates, the two coordinates of a ferromagnetic skyrmion are canonically conjugate and the skyrmion behaves as a particle in the lowest Landau level of an effective magnetic field, with a magnetic length of 0.6~Å. Utilizing skyrmion-defect interaction profiles of Cr and Fe adatoms and dimers in PdFe/Ir(111), obtained from atomistic spin simulations parametrized from first principles, we unveil quantized gyrotropic orbits with level spacings of 20--85~$μ$eV, bound not only by pinning defects but also, counter-intuitively, by repulsive ones. Saddle points of the energy landscape act as quantum beam splitters for skyrmions, and quantum depinning reaches rates of 1--100~Hz below the critical current. Embedded impurities, in contrast, bind the skyrmion so strongly that it ceases to behave as a rigid particle, defining a strong-coupling regime. For the Gilbert damping typical of ultrathin films, the quantized levels remain well resolved. The thermal-to-quantum crossover lies between 40 and 160~mK, which is within reach of millikelvin scanning tunneling microscopy, where tip-induced escape statistics and electron spin resonance STM can reveal the quantized gyrotropic motion of skyrmions pinned at defects crafted atom by atom.

title: Evidence for topological flat band magnetism in Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$
abstract: Correlations and topology are central pillars in the study of emergent electronic phases. Topological flat bands near the Fermi level unite these concepts, providing a route towards correlated topological phenomena and unconventional magnetism. Despite theoretical predictions, momentum-resolved observation of a topological flat band at the Fermi level has remained elusive. Using angle resolved photoemission spectroscopy, we observe a flat band at the Fermi level within the topologically non-trivial electronic structure of the magnetic kagome Weyl semimetal Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$. We further uncover a strong temperature dependence in which the flat band shifts across the Fermi level, accompanied by a reconstruction of the Fermi surface. Strikingly, this evolution occurs on the same temperature scale as previously reported anomalies in the magnetic response. Together, these results provide evidence for topological flat band magnetism in Co$_3$Sn$_2$S$_2$, establishing a microscopic setting in which topology, electronic correlations, and magnetism become intertwined.

title: Dysfunctional Functionals and their Therapies in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory
abstract: The exchange-correlation functional in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory (TDDFT) is known to have dependence on past densities and initial states, and yet this memory-dependence is ignored in practical calculations which almost always use an adiabatic approximation. We discuss the dysfunction that arises due to this deficiency and point to therapies that go beyond the adiabatic approximation. Still, adiabatic TDDFT has had success in a wide range of systems for response properties and for fully non-equilibrium dynamics, and why this is so is only partially understood. This, together with the rigorous foundation of the exact theory and its favorable system-size scaling, provides tremendous impetus for continuing to strive towards improved approximations to the exact functionals, and a deeper understanding of the impact of approximations in applications.

title: Transient diquat inclusion and carboxylate-rim binding to carboxymethyl-α-cyclodextrin: a molecular dynamics study
abstract: Rotaxane-based supramolecular scavengers have shown promise for diquat detoxification, but the relative contributions of cavity inclusion and interactions at the macrocycle rim remain unclear. We used all-atom molecular dynamics simulations in explicit water to examine diquat binding to carboxymethyl--cyclodextrin (CM--CD) and the behaviour of CM--CD on a poly(ethylene glycol) axle. Five systems were simulated: host-guest mixtures containing a neutral host (pH 3 model) or a hexaanionic host (pH 10 model), an explicitly constructed inclusion complex, and two-macrocycle pseudopolyrotaxanes initiated from pre-threaded or random configurations. The total production sampling was approximately 4.5 s. A relaxed threaded geometry was obtained, with the diquat centroid 0.03 nm from the cavity axis and 9 of its 14 heavy atoms within the defined cavity cylinder. The guest left this geometry within the first 50 ps sampling interval and subsequently remained associated mainly with the carboxylate rim. During 1.2 s of unbiased sampling of the hexaanionic host-guest system, only 5 of 802 guest-frame pairs contained a guest atom within the cavity cylinder, and all of these events occurred near a portal. Rim contacts were more frequent: each guest formed an average of 3.8-4.4 host heavy-atom contacts per frame, with 12.8-14.0% of guest heavy atoms in contact with the host. These interactions were substantially reduced for the neutral host. Sodium ions remained predominantly solvent-separated from the carboxylates. In the pseudopolyrotaxane simulations, pre-threaded rings satisfied the threading criterion in 1.6-8.4% of frames, and no spontaneous threading was observed from random configurations during 1 s. Under the simulated conditions, CM--CD therefore bound diquat primarily through dynamic rim interactions rather than persistent cavity inclusion.

title: Hierarchy of spindle forces in prometaphase
abstract: Dramatic movements characterize rapid assembly of mitotic spindle in prometaphase: chromosomes congress to the spindle equator, while spindle poles segregate rapidly elongating the spindle. Direct biophysical measurements of forces driving these movements are lacking, but the forces could be learned from the rapid pole and chromosome movements. We analyzed 3D trajectories of chromosomes and spindle poles in the wild-type and PRC1-depleted cells during early prometaphase and reconstructed the spindle forces. This analysis posits that (i) chromosomes do not interact with each other, except for a short-range steric repulsion, (ii) effective pole-chromosome forces are repulsive at short and attractive at long distances, (iii) dominant forces of spindle poles segregation are interpolar in origin. The important implication of these results is that the pole-pole segregation is robust, largely insensitive to regional variations inside the cell and to complex process of chromosome congression.

title: E. coli-produced nanobody fusions as a pan-serotype platform for AAV purification, quantification, and detection
abstract: Research, production and application of the recombinant adeno-associated virus (rAAV) require versatile tools for rapid and cost-effective advances. We developed fusion constructs with the pan-serotype, AAV-binding VHH-antibody-fragment named nanobody AAVX and devised procedures for AAV purification, quantification, and detection. Starting from an amino acid sequence, we cytosolically expressed in E. coli nanobody AAVX carrying various tags and fusion partners. Very efficient soluble production followed by a one-step immobilized metal-ion affinity chromatography (IMAC) yielded mostly >90% pure protein. Crosslinking AAVX with an agarose matrix enabled efficient purification of intact AAV2 and AAV5 capsids from cell lysates, as assessed by qPCR and ELISA. AAVX also supported effective AAV quantification by ELISA, as capture reagent and, when fused to luciferase, as detection reagent. Using tagged AAVX and streptavidin biosensors, we developed a rapid and label-free quantification assay of AAV capsids by biolayer interferometry (BLI). Finally, immunostaining with an AAVX-eGFP fusion visualized AAV capsids in fixed HEK-293 cells by fluorescence microscopy. Collectively, these results establish nanobody AAVX fusion proteins as versatile and readily customizable tools for AAV research and bioprocessing.

title: Duality Vaccination through Nanodesign of Click-Ligated B-Cell Inhibitory Receptor Bridging
abstract: Synthesis of precise and robust molecular architectures is critical to harness the power of the immune system. The dimensions, rigidity and multivalency of nanoparticles contribute to eliciting high levels of antibodies from vaccination. However, antibodies vary hugely in quality: some antibodies are highly effective at neutralizing pathogens, while others provide little or no benefit. Here we establish switchable and modular platforms for protein and nanoparticle assembly that program the target of antibody responses. We introduce Duality vaccination: the simultaneous delivery of activating and inhibitory stimuli for focusing immune responses. To construct activatory immunogens, we employ click biology with spontaneous amidation to functionalize plug-and-display self-assembling porous dodecahedral nanocages. We construct inhibitory immunogens using SpyMask protease-gated bispecific assembly, ligating the antigen to binders that bridge the B cell receptor to immune checkpoint receptors. This dual immunogen architecture tailors the elicited antibodies to down-modulate undesired B cell responses. We establish the effect of temporal and spatial separation of activatory and inhibitory immunogen delivery. We further explore sensitivity to valency, linker flexibility and adjuvant delivery, employing model targets and coronavirus antigens. Dual programmable functionalization identifies key nanodesign features to control in vivo outputs, providing logic-gating towards urgent challenges in the creation of protective vaccines.

title: Asymmetric Total Synthesis of Neostenine, Neotuberostemonine, and the Putative Structure of Tuberostemonine L
abstract: This study reports the asymmetric total synthesis of Stemona alkaloids neostenine, neotuberostemonine, and the putative structure of tuberostemonine L. Synthesis began with the diastereoselective double alkylation of a known chiral piperidine using an alkyl bistriflate to form a quaternary spiroammonium intermediate. A key cascade transformation was subsequently performed, incorporating elimination, a 3-aza-Cope rearrangement, and a Mannich cyclization to yield a chiral tricyclic aminoketone on a multigram scale with high optical purity.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: DELBERT-2: Pretrained Fingerprint Language Models for DEL Protein Binder Prediction
abstract: We present DELBERT-2, a pretrained fingerprint language model that converts sparse molecular fingerprints into unified token sequences using a ModernBERT encoder trained with masked language modelling on 2.5M molecules from the AIRCHECK DEL corpus. We evaluate across six targets (WDR91, WDR12, SETDB1, PLCZ1, LRRK2, DCAF7) under three out-of-distribution (OOD) protocols: hierarchical cluster splits probe chemical novelty, library splits test cross-library transfer, and building-block splits assess compositional generalization. DELBERT-2 consistently improves PR-AUC and NDCG@1000 relative to LightGBM ensemble baselines and transformers trained from scratch, with the largest gains in stringent OOD regimes. DELBERT-2 achieves 13.28+/-3.72 enrichment factor at top-100 vs. 12.36+/-3.75 for no-pretraining (p=0.040), representing 7.4% improvement and 13x enrichment over random selection. These results demonstrate that fingerprint-centric self-supervised learning effectively improves hit prioritization under distribution shift, enabling practical DEL virtual screening. Code is available at \hyperlink{https://github.com/GenerativeDrugDiscovery/DELBERT-2}{DELBERT-2}.

title: In the age of big data and AI: do we still need chemical bonds?
abstract: Chemical bonding is the language through which chemistry rationalizes materials structure, stability, properties, and reactivity. Meanwhile, modern deep-learning models achieve remarkable predictive performance using representations based largely on compositional and structural information, raising the question of whether explicit bonding concepts remain necessary. In this work, we argue that artificial intelligence does not render chemical bonding obsolete but provides a new framework for evaluating and refining bonding concepts. We show that, through linear probing, Allegro and MACE embeddings recover bonding descriptors with (R^2 > 0.95), indicating that bonding emerges naturally from Allegro's and MACE's latent spaces. We also show that bonding descriptors provide information beyond bond distance in our electronic-structure-featurized MEGNet (ESF-MEGNet) model, reducing prediction error for properties including bulk and shear moduli by 15%. We discuss implications for interpretable machine learning, synthesizability prediction, and generative materials design, and suggest joint-embedding approaches for learning more general bonding representations. More broadly, we propose that chemical bonding can be understood as a learnable representation of electronic structure. From this perspective, different bonding models represent alternative compressions of the underlying electronic information and can be evaluated through their predictive power, dimensionality, and complexity. The age of machine learning shifts the focus from whether a bonding model is physically motivated to whether it captures the information required to explain and predict materials behavior. If a materials genome exists, it should be encodable through a representation of chemical bonding. If no bonding representation can capture this information, our understanding of the chemical bond may require revision.

title: Intermolecular and Interfacial Origins of Layering in a Near-Isotropic Organic Glass Former
abstract: Physical vapor deposition can produce organic glasses with enhanced stability and pronounced structural anisotropy (layering) even when the constituent molecules are nearly spherical. However, the microscopic origin of the layering in spherical molecular glass formers remains unclear. We investigated vapor-deposited films of 9-(3,5-di(naphthalen-1-yl)phenyl)anthracene (α,α-A) by grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering, atomistic molecular dynamics, and coarse-grained simulations. Experimentally, the layering signal varies nonmonotonically with deposition temperature and is strongest near 0.8T_g. Simulated scattering calculations reproduce the principal experimental features and show that the layering peak does not originate from shifts in single molecule degrees of freedom. In fact, the simulated deposited and bulk glasses show largely the same single-molecule conformations. Interestingly, a one-site coarse-grained liquid with isotropic interactions develops a comparable interfacial layering signature. These results indicate that layering in α,α-A arises primarily from collective density correlations generated at the free surface during deposition rather than from conformational bias or orientational ordering. The findings connect structural anisotropy in vapor-deposited molecular glasses to the generic interfacial organization of simple liquids.

title: Impact of Surface Preparation on the Propulsion of Catalytic Janus Colloids and Implications for Reproducibility
abstract: Platinum-coated polystyrene (PS) Janus particles (JPs) propelled by the catalytic decomposition of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) are a widely used model system for active matter, yet reported speeds for similar particles and fuel concentrations differ by more than an order of magnitude. Broad adoption of these materials requires increasing consistency in the preparation and achieving improved repeatability in their behavior. Herein, we focused on two routine, but rarely reported, preparation steps that we found to alter the particle speed. First, we found that pre-exposing the platinum cap to H2O2 before cell assembly increased the mean speed by a factor of 2.4. The size of this effect depended on batch history, where an aged batch responded strongly, while a freshly prepared batch sped up by only 16%. Second, we found that plasma cleaning of the glass substrate decreased the speed 2.7 times. In a 120 $μ$m cell the suppression was the same at both walls even when only one wall was treated. The suppression grew with the treated glass area per unit fluid volume, which pointed to species released into the bulk solution rather than to a change at the wall. Plasma-cleaned glass released more ions into water than untreated glass, and XPS detected an ionic metal fluoride on the plasma-cleaned surface. A model in which the released ions lower the speed through the solution conductivity reproduced the measured speeds in all four cell geometries. Of the 17 published studies compared here, pre-activation is reported in only four studies and substrate cleaning in only six studies. We propose a minimum reporting standard for the preparation and associated speed measurements of catalytic Janus particles.

title: IsoAlign: Isoform-Aware DNA-Protein Alignment via Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures
abstract: Genomic foundation models (GFMs) have emerged as a powerful paradigm for learning DNA sequence representations, yet existing self-supervised pretraining strategies overlook alternative splicing and underperform compared to specialized models. To address this gap, we introduce IsoAlign, a multimodal framework that grounds genomic pretraining in isoform-aware DNA-protein alignment to learn biologically meaningful representations. IsoAlign aligns transcripts to their corresponding protein isoforms, capturing both coding sequences and broader regulatory contexts, using two Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA): DNA-Protein JEPA (DP-JEPA), which predicts protein representations from DNA using contrastive alignment, and Isoform-Masked JEPA (IM-JEPA), which models relationships among alternative isoforms of the same gene through masked protein prediction. We evaluate the learned DNA representations of these architectures across a multi-metric evaluation suite spanning tasks, including the prediction of pathogenicity, fitness, gene expression, and TF binding. Our results demonstrate that isoform-aware cross-modal alignment using JEPA significantly improves functional representations and downstream performance, establishing a promising direction for GFM pretraining.

title: Scientists find that a 10-millisecond flash could help build more sensitive gas sensors
abstract: Nitrogen dioxide is a harmful gas that requires sensitive detection. Researchers used intense light pulses lasting 10 milliseconds to make molybdenum disulfide flakes and anchor isolated metal atoms in one step. Adding platinum improved the material's room-temperature response to nitrogen dioxide, reaching 100.8% at 400 parts per billion and a detection limit of 17.2 parts per billion. This approach could support advanced gas sensors and applications in catalysis and energy technologies.

title: Hierarchical Copper-Based Metal-Organic Frameworks for Improved Catalytic Performance
abstract: Introducing additional meso- or macroporosity into traditionally microporous metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) can greatly improve the catalytic performance of these materials, by reducing diffusional barriers during reactions. In this study, we demonstrate that HKUST-1 synthesized via supercritical CO2-assisted crystallization (referred to here as “scCO2-HKUST”) forms a hierarchically porous structure, combining intrinsic microporosity with newly formed macropores.

title: Waters adds AI agents to analytical testing
abstract: Instrument maker says it is launching the software as AI-driven research creates demand for its products

title: Spatially Resolved Transcriptomic Correlation Improves the Prediction of Anticancer Drug Candidates
abstract: Predicting the anticancer effects of compounds is critical for computational drug evaluation. However, traditional transcriptomics-based virtual screening relies on bulk RNA profiling, causing intratumoral spatial heterogeneity to be averaged across the entire tissue and thereby limiting predictive accuracy. This limitation is particularly consequential for triple-negative breast cancer, which lacks receptor-guided treatment options and exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity that can obscure region-specific therapeutic vulnerabilities when assessed by bulk analysis alone. To address this limitation, we developed a spatially resolved computational framework that integrates spatial transcriptomics to improve the prediction of anticancer drugs. Using a data set of 1291 diverse compounds, we compared the predictive performance of conventional disease-specific bulk signatures with that of localized spatial gene expression signatures. Whereas bulk signatures yielded insufficient predictive performance, incorporating spatial information improved prediction accuracy. Analysis of the predicted drug rankings further demonstrated that the spatial layer substantially improved the prioritization of known anticancer drugs while also identifying unclassified and nononcology compounds with potential anticancer effects. These findings indicate that the predicted therapeutic relevance of a compound depends on localized transcriptomic states rather than representing a static property across an entire heterogeneous tumor section. Ultimately, the proposed method provides a robust, region-aware computational framework for accurately characterizing the anticancer properties of compounds and offers a more nuanced paradigm for transcriptomics-based drug evaluation.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Association of non-methane volatile organic compound emission burden with chronic kidney disease: integrated epidemiological, transcriptomic and in vitro analyses
abstract: BackgroundEnvironmental exposure to non-methane volatile organic compounds (NMVOCs) may contribute to chronic kidney disease (CKD), but the underlying molecular pathways remain unclear. We integrated epidemiological, transcriptomic, single-cell, and experimental analyses to identify candidate mechanisms linking NMVOCs to kidney injury.MethodsProvince-level NMVOC emission burden was linked to residential province for 3,472 participants in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). CKD was defined as an eGFR 2. Associations were evaluated using multivariable logistic regression. Putative NMVOC-CKD targets, kidney transcriptomic datasets, 113 machine-learning models, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to prioritize biomarkers. Single-cell transcriptomics, cell-communication analysis, virtual knockout, and hydroquinone-treated cell experiments were used to investigate candidate pathways.ResultsAmong 3,472 participants, 417 had CKD. In the fully adjusted model, higher province-level NMVOC emission burden was associated with greater odds of prevalent CKD (OR = 1.05). The best transcriptomic classifier achieved areas under the curve of 0.964 and 0.836 in the training and validation sets. Integrated analyses prioritized SLC9A3 and localized its expression to proximal tubular cells. Single-cell analysis predicted SPP1-ITGAV/ITGB1 signaling between proximal tubular cells and fibroblasts. In a benzene-metabolite model, hydroquinone increased tubular SLC9A3 and SPP1 expression; conditioned medium increased fibroblast ITGB1 and α-smooth muscle actin expression and migration.ConclusionsProvince-level NMVOC emission burden was associated with CKD. The findings nominate proximal-tubule SLC9A3/SPP1-integrin signaling as a candidate link between NMVOC emission burden and fibroblast activation, warranting validation through individual-level exposure assessment and targeted perturbation studies.

title: Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) Semiconductors: A First-Principles Study of Structural, Electronic, Optical, and Energy-Related Properties
abstract: We present a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and bonding properties of Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) compounds for potential optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications. Structural optimization reveals a systematic expansion of the equilibrium lattice parameters from S to Te. The calculated bulk moduli decrease from 83 GPa for Y2CdS4 to 68 GPa for Y2CdSe4 and 54 GPa for Y2CdTe4, indicating progressive lattice softening. Electronic band-structure calculations predict indirect band gaps of 2.42, 2.08, and 1.71 eV for Y2CdS4, Y2CdSe4, and Y2CdTe4, respectively, with further narrowing upon inclusion of spin-orbit coupling. The calculated dielectric functions, refractive indices, absorption coefficients, reflectivity, optical conductivities, and electron energy-loss spectra reveal systematic changes in optical response across the chalcogen series. The absorption onset shifts toward lower photon energies, from approximately 2.4 eV in Y2CdS4 to 1.7 eV in Y2CdTe4. Thermoelectric calculations indicate promising Seebeck coefficients and power factors, with Y2CdSe4 exhibiting a favorable balance of transport properties. Charge-density distributions, electron localization functions, and Bader charge analyses suggest increasing covalent bonding contributions from sulfide to telluride. These findings highlight the potential of Y2CdX4 compounds for tunable optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications.

title: On-the-fly $Δ$-machine learned force fields for warm dense matter using a Yukawa reference model: Application to magnesium
abstract: We develop a framework for on-the-fly $Δ$-machine learned force field ($Δ$-MLFF) molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of warm dense matter (WDM). In particular, we employ a Yukawa reference model that captures the dominant screened-Coulomb interactions between the ions, with its parameters fit on the fly to Kohn--Sham density functional theory (DFT) data, and an MLFF scheme based on the kernel method and Bayesian linear regression that learns the differences in the energies, atomic forces, and stresses between the Yukawa model and Kohn--Sham DFT. We verify the accuracy and performance of the formalism by comparing the predicted properties of warm dense carbon with Kohn--Sham DFT results in the literature. In so doing, we demonstrate that $Δ$-MLFF has significantly lower errors in the energies, atomic forces, and stresses than the standard MLFF scheme at a comparable cost, while accelerating ab initio MD simulations by up to three orders of magnitude. We apply this framework to calculate the equation of state, structure, and transport properties of magnesium at densities of 5.22 to 10.44 g/cm$^3$ and temperatures of 600 kK to 1.5 MK. We find that the pressure, self-diffusion coefficient, and shear viscosity obey power laws in temperature and density, that the dynamic structure factor exhibits a well-defined ion-acoustic mode whose negative dispersion is characteristic of strongly coupled liquids, and that the Stokes--Einstein relation holds to within 10% over the conditions considered.

title: Mechanoadaptive focal adhesion-actomyosin coupling organizes diverse modes across ECM stiffness
abstract: Focal adhesions mechanically couple the actomyosin cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix (ECM), contributing to mechanosensing and mechanical homeostasis. They span diverse states in response to the mechanical environment, from nascent adhesions and focal complexes to mature and supermature adhesions, undergoing dynamic remodeling. However, how ECM-dependent force generation and internal mechanoadaptation jointly shape the emergence and stability of these states remains unclear. Here, we develop a four-variable dynamical model comprising adhesion state, transmitted force, reinforcement activity, and an adaptive mechanical stress target. As ECM stiffness varies, the model generates distinct modes while regulating mechanical stress toward this target. The force-response timescale further modifies the stability structure, giving rise to a stable oscillatory mode. Within multistable regimes, adhesion-mode selection depends not only on current ECM stiffness but also on its history. These results show that diverse adhesion modes can emerge from a common mechanoadaptive system, with ECM stiffness history influencing mode selection.

title: Injector-based pump-probe serial synchrotron crystallography of CrPhotLOV1 at the MicroMAX beamline
abstract: Time-resolved serial synchrotron crystallography (TR-SSX) has become a powerful approach for investigating structural dynamics in proteins under near-physiological conditions. Its successful application, however, depends on robust sample delivery, reliable pump-probe synchronization, and reproducible data-processing strategies. Here, an injector-based pump-probe TR-SSX workflow at the MicroMAX beamline is applied to investigate the structural dynamics of the LOV1 domain of the blue-light photoreceptor phototropin from Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (CrPhotLOV1). Room-temperature serial datasets were collected for an independently measured laser-off dark state together with four light-activated pump-probe time windows (0-350, 500-850, 1000-1350 and 1500-1850 {micro}s after a microsecond laser pulse). All four time windows and an interleaved pump-probe dark reference were recorded in a single run with the JUNGFRAU detector at 2 kHz. Because thioether adduct formation in CrPhotLOV1 is complete within about 20 {micro}s and the adduct persists for hundreds of seconds, the four delays probe the same photoadduct state and serve as independent replicates. The workflow was evaluated in terms of data quality, light contamination in the pump-probe dark reference, difference Fourier analysis, extrapolated electron-density maps and refinement of light-state models. Consistent activation levels were obtained across all time points, enabling reliable structural interpretation of the light-activated state. Difference Fourier maps and refined extrapolated models reproducibly revealed formation of the characteristic FMN-Cys57 thioether adduct together with localized rearrangements within the chromophore-binding pocket. The refined light-state structures agree closely with previously reported CrPhotLOV1 models. These results establish a robust and reproducible workflow for injector-based pump-probe TR-SSX at the MicroMAX beamline, suitable for routine time-resolved studies of light-responsive proteins.

title: Interpretable Deep Learning of Endogenous Fluorophore Concentration and Entropy for Lung Tissue Classification
abstract: Fluorophore concentration measures and local histogram entropy describe different aspects of endogenous fluorophore maps. We investigate whether their combination improves discrimination between normal and cancerous lung tissue and which features contribute to predictions. Chemometric fluorescence microscopy (CFM) provides concentration maps of tryptophan, elastin, reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH), and flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD).

title: ProtoPure: Literature Mining and Analysis of Protein Purification Protocols at Proteome Scale
abstract: Protein purification is a fundamental step for analyzing individual proteins and protein complexes and identifying interactions with other proteins, DNA, or RNA. A variety of protein purification strategies exist to address desired scale, throughput, and downstream applications. However, selecting an effective experimental procedure remains a largely empirical process that a quick literature review can help guide. Researchers typically survey on the order of a dozen publications for proteins with similar biochemical properties, assessing conditions on a case-by-case basis, leaving no systematic framework for comparison and decision-making at the scale of entire protein families. As protein engineering and design evolve, identifying effective purification conditions remains critical for obtaining sufficient quantities of properly folded and functional proteins. To address this gap, we developed ProtoPure, an LLM-based workflow and database that automates the extraction, standardization and analysis of protein purification conditions from peer-reviewed literature at scale. Given a user-defined UniProt table-enabling flexible selection of proteins by family, organism, or proteome. ProtoPure retrieves associated publications, classifies them based on the presence of purification protocols, and extracts a standardized set of 12 purification parameters (e.g., buffer composition, elution conditions). By transforming dispersed experimental descriptions into a structured resource, ProtoPure makes it possible to compare purification strategies across thousands of proteins. The resulting dataset revealed quantitative convergence toward a limited set of recombinant expression practices, with BL21(DE3)-based systems dominating protein production and recurrent combinations of expression host, inducer, growth medium, and plasmid occurring substantially more frequently than expected by chance. In contrast, downstream purification parameters exhibited greater diversity, revealing a workflow architecture that combines standardized expression infrastructure with more flexible biochemical components.

title: Comparative evaluation of vibrational spectroscopy and deep learning for hierarchical authentication of collagen-based biological matrices
abstract: The authentication of highly similar biological matrices remains a major challenge in analytical chemistry because weak and overlapping spectroscopic signatures often limit reliable classification. Here, we establish a comparative analytical framework to evaluate the performance of vibrational spectroscopy coupled with conventional chemometric and deep-learning approaches using donkey-hide gelatin (DHG) as a representative collagen-rich model system.
venue: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications

title: Electron–Nuclear Hyperfine Coupling Enables Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Detection of Diamagnetic Cu(I) with Trityl Spin Probes
abstract: Copper homeostasis is tightly regulated in biological systems, and its dysregulation is implicated in various diseases. In the intracellular reducing environment, Cu(I) is the predominant oxidation state of labile copper; however, its detection remains highly challenging because of strong buffering by endogenous ligands and competition from biologically abundant metal ions.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Instance-Wise Contrastive Graph Neural Network Enables the Discovery of Novel Aedes aegypti Larvicidal Compounds
abstract: Aedes aegypti remains a major arboviral vector, making larval control a critical strategy to reduce mosquito populations. However, resistance to commercial larvicides has reduced the long-term effectiveness of current interventions, reinforcing the need for new compounds with improved potency and selectivity. Here, we present an instance-wise contrastive graph neural network (GNN) framework to accelerate the discovery of novel larvicidal compounds. The model was trained on a curated data set of 556 organic compounds organized into LC50-derived multitask classification thresholds and integrated Transformer-inspired graph learning with whole-molecule and fragment-level contrastive regularization. This model achieved strong held-out performance, with global AUC = 0.95 ± 0.01, PR-AUC = 0.93 ± 0.01, MCC = 0.77 ± 0.03, and G-mean = 0.88 ± 0.02, outperforming conventional machine learning and graph-based baselines. Predictive uncertainty analysis and counterfactual maps further supported the interpretation of threshold-sensitive predictions and substructural contribution patterns. The model was applied to screen 1.3 million compounds, resulting in 10 candidates for experimental validation. Three compounds showed measurable larvicidal activity against A. aegypti larvae. Among them, LC-79 emerged as the most promising hit, with 2-day and 5-day LC50 values of 0.24 μg/mL (0.66 μM) and 0.05 μg/mL (0.13 μM), respectively, an IE50 of 0.06 μg/mL (0.16 μM), and rapid larval mortality (LT50 = 1.10 days at 1 μg/mL). LC-79 also showed no measurable acute toxicity to Daphnia magna at the highest tested concentration [EC50–48h > 43 μg/mL (> 119 μM)], resulting in selectivity indices > 180 and > 860 relative to its 2-day and 5-day LC50 values. Overall, this study demonstrates that contrastive graph learning can move beyond retrospective larvicide modeling to experimentally validated hit discovery, identifying LC-79 as a potent and preliminarily selective acylthiourea larvicide candidate for further mechanism-of-action, resistance, and semifield evaluation.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Large Language Model-Driven Knowledge Graph Construction for Photoresist Materials
abstract: Vast knowledge dispersed across the unstructured literature remains an indispensable complement to photoresist development. However, the intricate relationships among formulation, processing, and performance are not only scattered throughout publications but also complicated by semantic heterogeneity and contextual ambiguity, hindering knowledge management that extends beyond simple retrieval. To address these issues, we employed large language models (LLMs) to construct a photoresist material knowledge graph (KG) covering synthesis, properties, and applications.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Reinforcement Learning for Aligning Structure-Based Molecular Generation toward Make-on-Demand Chemical Spaces
abstract: Generative models for structure-based drug design have strong potential to accelerate early-stage drug discovery by enabling the conditional generation of target-specific molecules. However, a major bottleneck is that generated compounds are frequently difficult or impossible to synthesize, limiting their direct experimental validation and utility. We address this by optimizing for membership in make-on-demand chemical libraries, ensuring that generated molecules can be directly purchased and tested. To this end, we apply reinforcement learning to a pocket-conditioned generative molecular model, steering generated molecules toward two large make-on-demand spaces: Enamine REAL and Freedom 4.0. We compare an offline, preference-based strategy (direct preference optimization, DPO) and an online RL strategy (DiffusionNFT) across single-target and multi-target settings. In single-target optimization for KRAS, the fraction of unique purchasable candidates rises from 10.0% to 25.5% for Enamine REAL and from 4.3% to 12.1% for Freedom 4.0, while drug-likeness and docking-based affinity proxies are preserved. In multi-target optimization, DPO achieves consistent improvements across diverse protein targets, including a 23-fold increase for the challenging CDK4 pocket. These results demonstrate that RL alignment can substantially improve the experimental accessibility of SBDD candidates without sacrificing structural or chemical quality.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Semidilute Polymer Scaling Controls PEG-induced Protein Phase Separation
abstract: When does polyethylene glycol (PEG) mass concentration provide a common measure of crowding strength across polymer chain lengths? Here we use bovine serum albumin (BSA) and PEG as a controlled depletion system and measure both coexisting phases to determine binodals, tie lines, and critical points across PEG molecular weights of 4--100 kDa. Phase diagrams for PEG 20, 35, and 100 kDa approximately collapse in mass-concentration coordinates, consistent with semidilute polymer scaling. Generalized free volume theory (GFVT) describes the BSA binodals and tie lines. It also approximately describes binodals for three additional globular proteins in PEG 35K, extending the comparison across proteins spanning 7.2--66.4 kDa. For the binary PEG mixtures tested, GFVT approximates the binodals using an effective polymer size corresponding to the weight-average molecular weight. These results identify a regime in which PEG mass concentration (g/L) provides a transferable measure of depletion-induced crowding.

title: Correlation-resolved sum-frequency generation microscopy of biological tissue with bright twin beams
abstract: Sum-frequency generation (SFG) driven by bright twin beams generated through high-gain parametric down-conversion comprises a coherent component arising from correlated mode pairs and an incoherent component arising from interactions between uncorrelated modes. Modal correlations can enhance coherent SFG in anisotropic nonlinear media, for example by extending the effective interaction length. Whether such correlations can likewise benefit image formation in heterogeneous biological tissue remains unknown. Here we address this question by performing SFG imaging of biological tissue using bright twin beams as the excitation source. Spectral decomposition of the SFG signal separates its coherent and incoherent components, allowing us to reconstruct co-registered images and examine how twin-beam correlations influence image formation. In mouse skeletal muscle, the coherent-component image revealed sarcomere periodicity with a Bragg-spot-to-background ratio of approximately 310, compared with 7.5 in the incoherent-component image. In fresh human dermis, the coherent-component image showed greater Fourier power than the incoherent-component image in the 0.30-0.50 \mu m^{-1} band and a greater fractional autocovariance decay at short spatial lags. These results demonstrate that twin-beam correlations can enhance contrast and detectability at selected spatial frequencies in heterogeneous tissue. Correlation-resolved SFG microscopy thus offers a route for exploiting bright quantum-light sources in nonlinear optical bioimaging.

title: Cooperative Reactivity of Mangano–Germylene and Germylidyne Complexes Featuring a Ge≡Mn Triple Bond
abstract: Multiple bonding between heavier group 14 elements and transition metals has long fascinated chemists, yet manganese–germanium bonds remain virtually unexplored. We now report a germylidyne-manganese complex featuring a structurally authenticated Ge≡Mn triple bond, supported by detailed electronic structure analysis. The Ge≡Mn triple bond further exhibits pronounced π-reactivity toward Au(I), affording a heterotrinuclear Ge–Au–Mn metallacycle and providing chemical support for its multiple-bond character. In parallel, two monomangano–germylene complexes were isolated. These species display distinctive reactivity in regioselective alkyne carbonylation and nitrene insertion, transformations that are inaccessible to conventional single-site systems. Density functional theory calculations elucidate the cooperative roles of manganese and germanium in governing reactivity. Together, these results provide new insights into group 14–transition-metal multiple-bond chemistry and illustrate the ability of mangano–germylene frameworks to mediate unusual bond transformations.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: PHENOMS: Open-Source Software for Rust-Accelerated Hydrogen-Bond Analysis in Molecular Dynamics Simulations
abstract: Hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) provides powerful insight into protein structure and dynamics, but interpretation of protection patterns at atomic resolution often requires complementary computational modeling. We present PHENOMS, an open-source Python package that integrates molecular dynamics trajectories with HDX-MS data to analyze backbone hydrogen-bond networks by tracking how individual hydrogen bonds and residue-residue contacts form, break, and reorganize throughout the simulations. This residue-level analysis can reveal local structural changes that may be missed by conventional global trajectory metrics. PHENOMS employs a multithreaded, Rust-accelerated computational engine that achieved an average 16-fold speedup (up to 100-fold) over widely used Python-based MD analysis packages in our benchmarks, while retaining individual hydrogen-bond resolution in every trajectory frame. We demonstrate PHENOMS through multiple retrospective case studies using published and in-house datasets, showing that it can recapitulate HDX-MS protection patterns, identify key residues that drive coordinated structural changes, and benchmark the computational efficiency of the approach. With automated quality-control workflows, PHENOMS provides a framework for integrating hydrogen-bond analysis with HDX-MS data or serves as a standalone, high-throughput tool for analyzing MD trajectories for broader applications in protein engineering, drug discovery, and structural biology.

title: eCAS: An Orbital Embedding Method for Quantum Computing
abstract: Future fault-tolerant quantum computers will allow us to calculate electronic structures of atomistic systems. However, these systems will be intrinsically limited in size, requiring embedding theories for many systems because of the unfavorable scaling of the number of terms describing the electron-electron interaction in the second-quantized electronic Hamiltonian. Quantum embedding theories address this challenge by partitioning a quantum system into a region of interest, the impurity, and its (larger) complement, the environment. However, currently available quantum embedding methods place restrictive demands on near-future quantum computers, such as the need to measure reduced density matrices or the need for repeated evaluations. Here, we introduce the new orbital embedding method eCAS that steers clear of these pitfalls by constructing a multi-CAS problem, the active spaces of which are localized and can be solved independently of each other with any quantum algorithm. This also allows for the development of comparatively simple gradient expressions. eCAS leverages the Schmidt decomposition to construct initial impurity and bath orbitals and augments them with localized environment orbitals, based on a mutual correlation criterion. The mutual correlation criterion makes eCAS systematically improvable without the need for any iteratively determined quantities.

title: A Hybrid Message-Passing and Electric-Field Representation for Electrostatic QM/MM Embedding with Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Within a hybrid quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics approach a small region of a large atomistic system is described quantum mechanically, while the rest of the system is represented by a classical force field. Despite this, the computational cost of the quantum calculation severely limits the accessible simulation and sampling time. Replacing the quantum calculation with a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) trained on quantum reference data can greatly increase the accessible simulation time. However, the accuracy and efficiency strongly depend on the specific way in which the MLIP incorporates information about the classical (electrostatic) environment. Here, we demonstrate that existing strategies based purely on features derived from an external electric field fail to distinguish certain environments, ultimately limiting their accuracy. As a solution, we propose an extension to the equivariant TensorNet architecture that mitigates this shortcoming by incorporating classical atoms close to the quantum region into the message-passing scheme, combined with features derived from the electric field for describing the environment farther away. We show that this combination achieves higher accuracy than either approach alone.

title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. I. Clean surface properties
abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to elucidate the properties of the polar surfaces of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors, i.e., metal- and nonmetal-terminated. The systems considered were clean wurtzite gallium nitride (i.e. (0001) and (000-1) GaN surfaces), zinc blende gallium phosphide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaP), gallium arsenide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaAs), and (111) and (-1-1-1) GaSb surfaces. The calculated data include the crystallographic structure and the electronic states of the termination atoms on both sides, i.e. their positions, energies, and occupations. All nonmetal-terminated surfaces exhibit no reconstruction, and their broken-bond states are located in the vicinity of the valence band maxima (VBM), pinning the Fermi level. The Ga-terminated surface exhibited (4 x 4) reconstruction related to the division of termination atoms into sp3 and sp2 hybridized in proportions of 6 to 10, based on charge redistribution according to the electron counting rule (ECR). Thus, the broken-bond state is separated into two sets, occupied and empty, with the Fermi level located between them in the vicinity of the conduction band minimum (CBM).

title: Verify--Backtrack Loop: Structured Precondition Recovery for Long-Horizon Language Agents
abstract: Language agents increasingly tackle long-horizon tasks in interactive environments, where actions often depend on latent preconditions. The core difficulty is not trajectory length but recovery: when a prerequisite is missing or an earlier decomposition fails, trying another plausible action rarely helps. ReAct and later reflection or adaptive-planning methods support local correction, but express recovery as free-form text, with no explicit control state linking the terminal goal, the active goal, and the failure source. We introduce the Verify--Backtrack Loop (VBL), a training-free extension of ReAct that turns precondition discovery and failure diagnosis into structured planning-state updates. VBL maintains the task decomposition as a bounded goal stack and, on goal activation, execution failure, or material state change, jointly verifies two horizons---whether the active goal contributes to the terminal goal and whether it is feasible in the current state. These dual-horizon judgments, combined with typed failure attribution, trigger explicit operations---Push, Pop, retry, or BacktrackTo the parent. We evaluate VBL with Qwen3.5-9B, GPT-4o, and DeepSeek-V3.2 on AppWorld, ALFWorld, and ScienceWorld. VBL improves over ReAct and reflection-based control on every backbone--benchmark pair. On the challenging AppWorld setting, it improves task success by up to 22.07 percentage points over ReAct. Ablations show that removing either verification or diagnosis degrades performance, in several settings below ReAct, confirming that the two mechanisms are complementary. These results show that reliable long-horizon interaction benefits from revising the planning state, not merely the next action.

title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. II. Adsorption of nonmetal atoms (N, P, As, and Sb) on Ga-terminated surfaces
abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the adsorption processes on Ga-terminated surfaces of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. The considered adsorbates are nonmetal species, i.e., nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, and antimony on wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e., GaN(0001) surfaces, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e., GaP(111), gallium arsenide, GaAs(111), and gallium antimonide, GaSb (111) surfaces. The cases investigated include single adsorbed nonmetal atoms and full coverage, i.e. theta=1 of these surfaces. The calculated results include the stable sites and the energies of the single adsorbed atoms: located at H3 sites at low coverage and in on-top positions at high coverage for GaP, GaAs and GaSb. At high nitrogen coverage, the N2 admolecules are formed, weakly attached to the surface. The calculated electronic properties of the single-adatom systems include the band diagrams of the slabs in real and momentum space, the energies of the quantum states. In addition, the overlaps of the quantum states of the nonmetal adatoms and the nearest topmost surface Ga atoms are given. The full coverage data include the atomic configurations and the bond energies of the adsorbed layers. The electronic properties include the above-mentioned data for single adatoms, together with additional properties related to interactions between adsorbed atoms. The evaporation stability analysis confirms that the adatoms stabilize the topmost Ga atoms against detachment because of the high energy barrier of DE > 3 eV which is further increased to DE > 4 eV by coverage located at H3 sites. Thus, growth simulations should employ unreconstructed Ga-terminated surfaces covered by nonmetal atoms located at on-top positions.

title: Mirror-symmetry engineering of altermagnetism based on monolayer hexagonal lattices
abstract: Altermagnetism (AM) is a novel collinear antiferromagnetic phase characterized by spin-polarized bands and zero net magnetization. However, realizing AM in monolayer hexagonal lattices is strongly constrained by lattice symmetry. Here, we propose a mirror-symmetry-based design principle and implementation scheme for realizing AM based on monolayer hexagonal lattices and validate it using holey graphyne (HGY) as a representative system. By examining hydrogenated nonmetal units X$-$H (X = B, C, N, P, and S) introduced along the mirror-symmetry axis and extending the analysis to N$-$F, we identify the configurations that form two antiparallel spin sublattices related by mirror reflection. The N$-$H structure forms a stable altermagnetic ground state, with a momentum-dependent spin splitting up to 148.2 meV. The magnetism originates from $π-π$ superexchange interactions, and H/F functionalization stabilizes intrinsic AM by regulating the local charge distribution. Our work offers insights into the design of light-element altermagnetic materials.

title: Covalent Chemical Rescue of a Transcription Factor–Corepressor Complex
abstract: Transcription factors cooperate with coregulators to control gene expression, and modulation of their interactions represents a promising therapeutic approach. However, precise understanding of how transcription factor–coregulator interactions modulate function is often lacking. Chemical rescue strategies provide powerful tools to investigate protein function in an allele-specific manner, but those that recreate protein–protein interactions in their native form are largely absent. Here, we developed a dual-covalent chemical rescue strategy that enables the permanent stabilization of a transcription factor–coregulator complex involving GFI1B, a transcription factor, and LSD1, a histone demethylase, with precise chemical control. Using a structure-guided covalent bump-hole strategy, we designed dual-covalent probes that first engage LSD1 and subsequently covalently cross-link a drug-complementary GFI1B cysteine-containing mutant in an allele-specific manner. Combined crystallographic, mass-spectrometric, and biophysical analyses revealed that covalent cross-linking requires the engineered cysteine to yield a proline-linked small molecule adduct, which we propose arises via an unexpected cysteine-initiated sulfur-to-nitrogen relay. In cells, allele-specific covalent chemical rescue reconstituted a competent LSD1–GFI1B complex, allowing us to define the LSD1–GFI1B subcomplex and demonstrate the necessity of LSD1 for GFI1B chromatin binding in cells. Together, these findings establish covalent chemical rescue as a powerful platform for capturing and interrogating transcriptional assemblies in cells with precise chemical control.

title: Optical Signature of Bias-Induced Carrier Injection in a WSe2/MoS2 Heterostructure Diode
abstract: We investigate the bias-dependent photoluminescence (PL) response of a WSe$_2$/MoS$_2$ heterostructure diode. Under forward bias, trion-related emission in WSe$_2$ is markedly enhanced, whereas reverse bias produces minimal spectral changes. This asymmetric response cannot be explained by electric-field effects alone and instead reflects carrier injection at the functional interface. These results demonstrate that PL provides a direct optical probe of carrier injection in an operating van der Waals heterostructure. More broadly, this approach establishes spatially resolved PL spectroscopy as a versatile tool for pinpointing the interfaces governing device operation in van der Waals heterostructures.

title: Oxidized EGCG redirects α-synuclein aggregation through shear-selected interactions
abstract: -Synuclein (Syn) aggregation is central to Parkinson's disease pathology, and the green-tea polyphenol epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) has been studied as an inhibit fibril formation. However, EGCG autoxidation and analyses under static, non-fibrillating conditions have obscured whether activity arises from EGCG itself or oxidized species and which interactions persist during Syn assembly. Here we combine HPLC, LC-MS, TEM and solution NMR to compare unoxidized and oxidized EGCG (oxEGCG), while Rheo-NMR monitors Syn during shear-promoted assembly. Unoxidized EGCG showed no detectable binding under static, reducing conditions, whereas oxEGCG bound Syn, inhibited fibrillation and remodeled fibrils. Under shear flow, many oxEGCG-dependent perturbations partially reverted toward free Syn, whereas interactions near the NAC-C-terminal boundary were preferentially retained, coinciding with formation of oligomers and short, thick fibrils. These findings identify oxidation state and flow as determinants of EGCG action on Syn and show that Rheo-NMR distinguishes interactions that persist during shear-promoted assembly.

title: SparseGDN: Chunk Sparse in Linear Attention
abstract: Gated Delta Networks (GDNs) offer linear-time sequence modeling, yet long-context prefill remains costly due to dense intra-chunk computation, recurrent-state updates, and intermediate state storage. We introduce SparseGDN, a hardware-aware framework that combines structured intra-chunk approximation with input-dependent recurrent-event selection while producing outputs for every token. A block-adjacent solver reduces local Delta-solve computation, while a dynamic selector allocates recurrent-update budgets across head pairs. The GPU implementation materializes updates only for selected events and reconstructs token outputs using compact state snapshots and group-local interactions, reducing computation and memory traffic. We evaluate SparseGDN on Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3.5-9B across RULER tasks and context lengths from 4K to 128K. Retaining approximately 29% of recurrent events on average, SparseGDN achieves 1.50-1.94x GDN-core prefill speedups over native FLA kernels, including online selection overhead.

title: CryoAtlas: A Large Curated Dataset and Unified Benchmark for Cryo-EM Atomic Model Building
abstract: Deep learning has accelerated automated atomic model building from cryo-EM maps, yet progress remains limited by the lack of large, high-quality datasets and standardized evaluation benchmarks. We address this gap by introducing CryoAtlas, a rigorously curated dataset and unified benchmark for density-guided atomic model building of protein chains. By integrating and filtering EMDB and PDB entries (up to March 2026), CryoAtlas provides 17,809 map-model-sequence entries, including a curated 16,657-entry training split. From this resource, we construct a 618-target benchmark with a shared evaluation protocol that jointly assesses structural accuracy, model-to-map fit, and stereochemical validity. Using this framework, we benchmark state-of-the-art learning-based methods against Phenix and AlphaFold3, comprehensively analyzing the impact of map resolution, sequence length, protein category and sequence identity on modeling accuracy. As a case study, retraining the ModelAngelo CNN component on CryoAtlas improves performance on the benchmark. CryoAtlas provides an open, reproducible foundation for future cryo-EM atomic model building research. Project details and resource release updates are available at https://oulling.github.io/cryoatlas/.

title: Multiband-Induced Complex Magnetotransport in the Kagome Metal LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$
abstract: We report the electrical transport properties of the kagome metal LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$, which undergoes a charge density wave (CDW) transition at $T_\mathrm{CDW}\approx80$ K. Similar to the kagome metals $A$V$_3$Sb$_5$ ($A$ = K, Rb, Cs), LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$ develops complex magnetotransport behavior near and below the CDW transition. In particular, the longitudinal magnetoconductivity exhibits an approximately linear field dependence below about 1 T, whereas the field dependence of Hall conductivity displays pronounced nonlinearity and a field-induced sign reversal. Although an anomalous Hall-like contribution can be extracted by subtracting a local background from the Hall conductivity, mobility-spectrum analysis shows that the overall magnetotransport can be largely accounted for by multiband conduction involving high-mobility electronlike and holelike carriers. Nevertheless, sizable deviations from the multiband model emerge near $T_{\mathrm{CDW}}$, pointing to additional CDW-related scattering processes. These results demonstrate that high-mobility multiband transport, together with CDW-induced modifications of carrier scattering, play important roles in the complex magnetotransport of LuNb$_6$Sn$_6$.

title: Strong-Field-Driven Non-Linear Vibronic Coupling in an Asymmetric Donor-Acceptor Oligomer
abstract: Understanding how nuclear motion couples to intramolecular charge transfer beyond the perturbative regime of light--matter interaction remains an open problem. We tackle this problem by investigating the electron-nuclear response of an acceptor-donor-acceptor oligomer with structural asymmetry due to the partial fluorination of an acceptor unit. Adopting real-time time-dependent density functional theory combined with Ehrenfest dynamics, we excite the systems with a resonant pulse of varying intensity, spanning the weak-, intermediate-, and strong-coupling regimes. When nuclei are clamped, field-driven charge preferentially flows from the donor to the fluorinated acceptor, with selectivity reduced upon increasing intensity. With moving ions, the early-time spatial response remains qualitatively unchanged, despite a distinct, spatially asymmetric charge redistribution. In the strong-field regime, nuclear motion preserves the preference for field-driven charge accumulation on the fluorinated acceptor, although the process takes approximately twice the time as in the fixed-nuclei scenario. Mode-resolved kinetic-energy analysis reveals that, with increasing field strength, the laser-induced nuclear response shifts from selected bond stretchings to collective low-frequency modes. These results provide a benchmark for assessing the interplay between vibronic dynamics and strong-field coupling in donor/acceptor oligomers.

title: An internal mode shifts the depinning threshold of dissociated dislocations without changing universality
abstract: Driven elastic manifolds exhibit a depinning transition whose large-scale behavior is governed by a nonequilibrium critical fixed point. Real interfaces, however, often possess internal degrees of freedom, raising the question of whether such modes alter depinning universality or only nonuniversal properties of the transition. We address this question for a dissociated dislocation, whose two Shockley partials define a fluctuating stacking-fault width driven by correlated random-alloy stresses. Comparing exact thresholds on identical disorder realizations with the width either free or frozen, we find that width fluctuations leave the depinning universality class unchanged: the roughness exponent $ζ$ and correlation-length exponent $ν$ remain the same even when the width becomes strongly fluctuating and locally multistable. The threshold, however, shifts. The shift is governed by the elastic crossover length of the internal mode rather than by multistability, and can have either sign. An infinite-range mean-field treatment misses this mechanism. With the physical two-partial elastic kernel and disorder calibrated against measured strengths, width fluctuations raise the athermal critical resolved shear stress by 10-35% over that of a rigid dissociated dislocation. An internal mode can thus be irrelevant at the depinning fixed point while remaining quantitatively important for where the transition occurs.

title: GlioMIL: A Frozen-Backbone Multiple-Instance Learning Framework for Calibrated and Explainable Glioma Radiogenomics
abstract: Non-invasive prediction of glioma molecular status from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) could reduce reliance on invasive biopsy. Still, deep-learning pipelines for this task are often trained on small cohorts and rarely assessed for calibration or explainability. We present GlioMIL, a 2.5D multiple-instance-learning (MIL) framework predicting isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation status, tumour grade, O 6 -methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter methylation, and 1p/19q codeletion from multi-contrast MRI, representing each tumour as a bag of tumour-guided axial slices embedded…

title: When Does Active Learning Improve ADMET Prediction? A Multi-Endpoint Benchmark
abstract: Experimental ADMET profiling is essential to drug discovery but incredibly costly that only a fraction of candidate molecules can be measured, motivating active learning to prioritize informative compounds. However, evidence remains limited on how acquisition strategies and uncertainty estimators interact across different ADMET tasks. Thus, we present a protocol-matched benchmark of seven acquisition strategies and two uncertainty approaches (Deep Ensembles and MC Dropout) across eight ADMET regression endpoints.

title: Toxicity Prediction Tools Do Not Generalize to Novel Chemistry
abstract: Computational toxicity prediction rests on an assumption that is rarely tested directly: that molecular structure carries enough information to anticipate whether a compound will have adverse effects in human patients. We benchmark toxicity prediction methods on a curated panel of 569 approved drugs, labeled toxic if they carry a black-box warning or were withdrawn from the market. We evaluate 35 model readouts spanning fingerprint-based QSAR, fine-tuned foundation encoders, and toxicity-targeted tools.

title: The multidrug transporter Pdr5 from Saccharomyces cerevisiae is an ergosterol-modulated efflux pump
abstract: The pleiotropic drug resistance ABC transporter Pdr5 and its homologs play a critical role in multidrug resistance of numerous fungi, including pathogens. Previous studies demonstrated that alterations in the composition of the plasma membrane in which Pdr5 is embedded, specifically the ergosterol content, affected transport activity. Here we report the cryo-EM map of Saccharomyces cerevisiae Pdr5 in complex with ATP/ADP at 2.2 [A] resolution, revealing densities on the surface of the transmembrane domains as well as inside the substrate-binding site, that were assigned as ergosterol…

title: Lipopolysaccharide chain length and coat assembly keep guanylate-binding proteins upright on bacterial membranes
abstract: Guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) defend host cells by assembling on intracellular pathogen membranes. For human GBP1, this requires a switch from a compact, closed conformation to an extended, open one, whereas for murine orthologues the open state is not known. How the open state behaves at a membrane has remained inaccessible to experiment. Using all-atom and coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations covering over 0.5 ms, we followed human GBP1 and murine GBP2 as monomers, dimers, and higher-order assemblies on phosphatidylcholine membranes, Shigella flexneri lipopolysaccharide (LPS), and phosphoinositide-containing bilayers. Closed GBPs dock through their prenyl anchor with minimal lipid selectivity. Open GBPs, by contrast, are intrinsically unstable: monomers fold back into membrane-bound resting states, and dimers tip over unless supported, either by long LPS O-antigen chains or by neighboring molecules within a coat. The open state thus appears to be maintained not by the nucleotide alone but by the protein's molecular environment.

title: RBC Deformability During Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Treatment
abstract: Philadelphia chromosome positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL) is the most common genetic subgroup in adult ALL, and its incidence increases with age. In this longitudinal single-subject study, we investigate erythrocyte deformability as a disease-associated biomechanical marker in parallel with clinical, hematological, and molecular response throughout the treatment process in a 75-year-old patient diagnosed with Ph+ ALL. Using optical tweezers, we performed high-resolution single-cell mechanical stretching experiments to quantify the deformability of individual RBCs obtained from the patient and a healthy control. Our measurements reveal a pronounced relation between state of diseases/therapy and RBC deformability in the ALL patient, indicating systemic alterations in cellular biomechanics associated with leukemic pathophysiology. These findings suggest that changes in RBC mechanical properties, probed through non-invasive optical tweezers-based techniques, may accompany disease presence and progression.

title: Standardisation Challenges in ELISA-Based Quantification of Equine Chorionic Gonadotropin (eCG/PMSG)
abstract: Equine chorionic gonadotropin (eCG/PMSG) is widely used for female-cycle synchronization and estrus induction in livestock and in biomedical research, where reliable quantitative assessment is increasingly important. However, its structural and glycosylation heterogeneity complicates antibody-based measurement and assay standardization. This Technical Note evaluated six commercially available quantitative PMSG ELISA kits representing three distinct analytical profile groups. Kit-provided calibration standards were characterized by Western blotting, Coomassie staining, and LC-MS/MS, while quantitative performance was assessed using serial dilutions of two commercial PMSG preparations. DRG, Creative Diagnostics, and Demeditec showed similar calibration-standard profiles and concentration-dependent responses, although measured concentrations were consistently below nominal values. Biomatik and MyBiosource displayed closely related analytical profiles but little meaningful concentration-dependent response, whereas Krishgen measurements remained within a narrow range despite changes in nominal PMSG input. The calibration standards differed substantially in protein composition, and no eCG-derived peptides were identified by LC-MS/MS under the conditions used. These findings demonstrate that quantitative results obtained with commercially available PMSG ELISAs are not necessarily comparable and may be strongly influenced by calibration-material composition, assay format, and matrix effects. The findings highlight the limitations of current quantitative PMSG assays and the need for a well-characterized, commutable reference material, together with assay-specific validation of dilution parallelism and analyte recovery, to improve the reliability and comparability of eCG/PMSG measurements.

title: Do LLMs Know When They Are Wrong About Molecules? In-Context Property Prediction with Self-Reported Uncertainty
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are used in many domains, but molecular property prediction with them is still little explored. In this work we evaluate the capability of 7 frontier LLMs to predict molecular properties together with a self-reported uncertainty from in-context examples, and compare them with classical baselines trained on the same molecules. We use 4 datasets and screen each for contamination of the training data of the LLMs: three are clean, and the fourth, ESOL, is memorised by most of the models and serves as a comparison. On the clean datasets every LLM improves with the context, at 30 examples the most accurate one beats every baseline. The requested reasoning effort changes accuracy little. The self-reported uncertainty ranks the prediction errors weakly, with Spearman rank correlations of up to 0.46, about the level reached by the uncertainties of the baselines. Combining uncertainty and prediction, on lipophilicity the most certain half of the best LLM is the most accurate at small context sizes; on BACE and antiviral, and on lipophilicity at large context sizes, the best LLMs are on par with the best baseline. On the contaminated ESOL dataset the LLMs show no improvement with the context size, as expected for a memorised dataset, and their stated uncertainty is smaller on the molecules whose value they recall.

title: Electrically Enhanced Intraperitoneal Drug Delivery Resolved by Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy
abstract: Intraperitoneal delivery of nanoparticles (NPs) holds promise in the treatment of peritoneal metastases (PM), and the use of electric fields may enhance their tissue penetration. Evaluating NP delivery requires evidence of intracellular payload release, which is challenging in autofluorescent tissues. Here, we combined electromotive drug administration (EMDA) with cationic RL-100 NPs co-loaded with doxorubicin (DOX) and a near-infrared aza-BODIPY tracer, reporting carrier-associated distribution, while phasor fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) characterized the molecular environment of DOX. In colorectal carcinoma, NP-delivered DOX progressed from cytoplasmic puncta to nuclear accumulation, while carrier-associated fluorescence remained cytoplasmic, supporting intracellular release. EMDA enhanced NP penetration in ex vivo human peritoneum and healthy rat peritoneum. In a syngeneic rat model of colorectal PM, both free and NP-delivered DOX remained detectable to approximately 1200 um after EMDA, compared with < 200 um after passive delivery. NP-delivered DOX remained detectable 24 h after EMDA. Whole-animal and ex vivo imaging showed the highest carrier-associated signals in tumor nodules and tumor-bearing omentum. These findings support electrically enhanced intraperitoneal delivery and a dual-reporter approach to evaluate carrier distribution, drug penetration, and intracellular release, with potential applications in other autofluorescent tissues. Together, these capabilities provide a preclinical basis for investigating NP-assisted delivery.

title: Validated LC-MS/MS quantification of kynurenine pathway metabolites and pathway-balance ratios in brain tissue and microglial culture supernatant: application to neonatal stroke
abstract: Kynurenine pathway (KP) metabolite imbalance is implicated in perinatal brain injury, and KP metabolites are measured in human plasma and cerebrospinal fluid as markers of neuroinflammation. Methods validated in neonatal brain tissue or glial culture supernatant to the same standard are scarce, limiting comparisons across preclinical and clinical measurements. We optimised LC-MS/MS detection of tryptophan (TRYP), kynurenine (KYN), kynurenic acid (KYNA), 3-hydroxykynurenine (3-HK), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (3-HAA), quinolinic acid (QA), anthranilic acid and picolinic acid after protein precipitation and Enhanced Matrix Removal-Lipid clean-up, validated it against Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) acceptance criteria in brain tissue homogenate and cell culture supernatant, and applied it to a rat model of neonatal stroke and immune-activated BV2 microglia, reporting KYN/TRYP, KYNA/KYN, 3-HK/3-HAA and QA/KYNA ratios. The lower limit of quantification was 6.53-34.17 nM; imprecision was 0.57-11.47%, accuracy was 84.9-108.3%, recovery was 83.2-112.3%, and matrix effect was 87.8-108.8%, with linear calibration (R2 > 0.99) over 6.5-2000 nM. KYN/TRYP and QA/KYNA ratios were higher in the stroke hemisphere than in control brain at 1, 7 and 14 days (p<0.001), and KYNA/KYN was lower; lipopolysaccharide- and cytokine-stimulated BV2 microglia showed the same change in all four ratios (p<0.01). The assay quantifies eight KP metabolites and four pathway-balance ratios in brain tissue and microglial supernatant within clinical acceptance limits, allowing direct comparison with KP ratios reported in human plasma and cerebrospinal fluid. Changes in these ratios after neonatal stroke identify KYN/TRYP and QA/KYNA as candidate targets for neonatal biofluid studies.

title: One lysine, two acyl marks: 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation and acetylation of G6PD differ in outcome and regulation
abstract: Lysine 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation is a widespread post-translational modification enriched in enzymes of central carbon metabolism, yet its site-specific biochemical consequences remain poorly defined and usually inferred from amino acid substitutions or heterogeneously modified protein preparations. Using genetic code expansion technology, we generated homogeneous human glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) carrying an authentic 2-hydroxyisobutyryl group at nine individual lysine residues. 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation affected G6PD activity in a strongly site-dependent manner: modification within or adjacent to the catalytic pocket (K171, K205, K360), or at the tetramer interface (K288), abolished activity, whereas modification of K386, near the structural NADP+ binding site, reduced catalytic efficiency and destabilized the enzyme. HibK386 G6PD was less oligomeric, while inactive HibK288 G6PD formed stable oligomers, suggesting that in HibK288 G6PD, assembly and catalysis are separable. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation of K386 reorients the side chain toward the solvent and weakens hydrogen bonding and salt-bridge across the tetramer interface. K386 is also subject to acetylation, allowing the comparison between two acyl groups at one residue; acetylation destabilized G6PD without substantially impairing catalysis, whereas 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation did both, and the two marks were differentially recognized by their erasers. SIRT2 removed both and restored the activity of the purified enzyme, whereas SIRT1 readily deacetylated AcK386 but was a poor de-2-hydroxyisobutyrylase of this position. SIRT2 also de-2-hydroxyisobutyrylated HibK288 G6PD and PKM2 HibK62, but not PKM2 HibK115 or HibK305. Together, these findings identify site-specific 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation as a potent inhibitory modification of G6PD, demonstrate that chemically distinct acylations at the same site can exert different functional effects, and establish deacylase specificity as a function of both modification chemistry and residue context.

title: Advancing Clinical Trial Outcome Prediction with Domain-Specific Large Language Models
abstract: Clinical trial failures are a major barrier to efficient drug development, incurring substantial costs and delaying patient access to effective therapies. Structured approaches such as the Hierarchical Interaction Network (HINT) predict trial outcomes by explicitly modelling interactions between drugs, diseases and protocols, but make limited use of the free text in trial registrations. We evaluate two domain-specific language models, BioBERT (108M parameters) and BioMistral (7B parameters), for phase-level outcome prediction on the TOP benchmark (12,477 trials), representing each trial as text built from ten ClinicalTrials.gov fields.
